security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown code fences and illustrative Docker or Kubernetes snippets, not executable skill behavior. I confirmed the hardcoded build-time network call to an external scan endpoint and added semantic findings for overbroad RBAC and disabled read-only root filesystems. No prompt injection evidence was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.suggestion: Remove the urllib request to security-scan.example.com or replace it with a documented local scanner and explicit user configuration.
Do not grant get, list, or watch on secrets to broad roles or default service accounts. Create narrow namespace Roles for each workload.
Set readOnlyRootFilesystem to true and mount explicit writable volumes for tmp, cache, and application state paths.

remediation.issue: Production examples need current Kubernetes review
remediation.suggestion: Label placeholders clearly and test manifests against supported Kubernetes APIs before recommending production use.

semantic_findings.title: Overbroad Kubernetes RBAC Grants Secret Read Access
semantic_findings.description: The ClusterRole grants get, list, and watch on secrets, then binds the role to the default service account in production. Workloads using that account could read sensitive Kubernetes secrets beyond their needs.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The YAML explicitly includes secrets in a ClusterRole and binds it to the default service account. This is a well-known privilege expansion risk in Kubernetes.

semantic_findings.title: Writable Root Filesystem in Security-Hardening Example
semantic_findings.description: The deployment sets readOnlyRootFilesystem to false at the pod and container levels, and the checklist also accepts a writable root filesystem. This weakens runtime containment for a security-focused example.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The manifest and checklist directly show readOnlyRootFilesystem as false. Legitimate writable paths should be mounted explicitly instead of leaving the root filesystem writable.

content.user_title: Build Secure Docker and Kubernetes Deployments
content.value_statement: Container teams need secure Docker and Kubernetes patterns that do not miss production controls. This skill provides hardened examples for images, workloads, GitOps, networking, and monitoring.
actual_capabilities: Guides multi-stage Dockerfile patterns with non-root users, health checks, and image cleanup.
Provides Kubernetes namespace, RBAC, NetworkPolicy, deployment, and service account examples.
Shows Istio service mesh configuration with mutual TLS, routing, and traffic policies.
Outlines ArgoCD GitOps application settings, sync behavior, and deployment sources.
Includes Prometheus alert examples for Kubernetes pods, services, and security events.
Supplies a production checklist covering security, observability, recovery, testing, and performance.
limitations: It provides examples only; it does not deploy, scan, or modify clusters by itself.
Some manifests require updates for current Kubernetes versions and provider policies.
Placeholder URLs, domains, account identifiers, and tokens must be replaced before use.
Security recommendations require review by platform and security teams before production.

use_cases.title: Create a Hardened Container Build
use_cases.description: Use the Dockerfile patterns to design a smaller image with non-root execution, health checks, and controlled runtime dependencies.

use_cases.title: Prepare Production Kubernetes Manifests
use_cases.description: Use the Kubernetes sections to draft namespaces, network policies, deployments, probes, service accounts, and resource settings.

use_cases.title: Review Cloud-Native Security Controls
use_cases.description: Use the checklist and examples to review RBAC, secrets, service mesh, observability, and compliance controls before release.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Dockerfile
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Dockerfile for production security. Focus on base image choice, package installation, user permissions, health checks, and image size.

prompt_templates.title: Draft Kubernetes Manifests
prompt_templates.prompt: Create Kubernetes deployment guidance for my web service. Include namespace, service account, resource limits, probes, security context, and network policy notes.

prompt_templates.title: Design a GitOps Release Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a GitOps workflow for a production Kubernetes application using ArgoCD. Include repository layout, sync policy, rollback approach, and approval controls.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Platform Baseline
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this Docker and Kubernetes platform baseline for zero-trust readiness. Prioritize RBAC, secrets, service mesh, runtime security, monitoring, and recovery gaps.

output_examples.input: Review a Python API Dockerfile for production readiness.
output: A prioritized hardening review with non-root runtime recommendations.
Image build improvements for dependency handling, cleanup, and health checks.
A short list of changes that need security team approval.

output_examples.input: Plan Kubernetes manifests for a secure web workload.
output: A deployment outline covering namespace, service account, resource requests, probes, and pod security settings.
Network policy guidance for ingress, egress, DNS, and service dependencies.
Notes about provider-specific identity and secret management choices.

output_examples.input: Assess whether our production checklist is complete.
output: A gap summary across container security, RBAC, secrets, observability, recovery, and testing.
Clear priority levels for controls that block production release.
Follow-up questions for platform owners and security reviewers.

best_practices: Treat every manifest as a starting point and adapt it to your cluster version, provider, and threat model.
Keep secrets, identity, RBAC, and network policy review separate from general deployment review.
Test hardening changes in staging before applying them to production workloads.
anti_patterns: Copying placeholder domains, account identifiers, tokens, or repository URLs into production manifests.
Granting broad ClusterRole permissions when a narrow namespace Role is enough.
Disabling runtime restrictions because an application needs one writable directory.

faq.question: Does this skill deploy containers or Kubernetes manifests automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples for an AI assistant to use during planning, review, and documentation.

faq.question: Can I use the examples directly in production?
faq.answer: No. Replace placeholders, remove unsafe defaults, and validate each manifest against your cluster, provider, and policies.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it cover both Docker and Kubernetes?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes Docker build patterns, Kubernetes manifests, service mesh examples, GitOps settings, monitoring, and a checklist.

faq.question: Does it replace a security review?
faq.answer: No. It helps prepare and structure reviews, but security teams must approve production controls.

faq.question: What should I check before using its Kubernetes examples?
faq.answer: Check API versions, RBAC scope, secret handling, network policies, provider identity settings, and runtime filesystem restrictions.
